en: aquiline nose; hooked nose; Roman nose

examples.en: That actor's hooked nose is his charm point.
I take after my father, so I have a hooked nose.
Many of my friends worry about their hooked noses.

examples.ko: 코가 매의 부리처럼 휘어서 매부리코라고 불러요.
examples.en: The nose curves like a hawk's beak, so it's called a hooked nose.

examples.ko: 성형 상담에서 매부리코를 펴고 싶다고 말했어요.
examples.en: At the consultation, I said I wanted to straighten my hooked nose.
Glasses slide down easily on a hooked nose.

explain: 코끝이 아래로 휘어진 코를 말하고, 반대로 코끝이 위로 들린 코는 '들창코'라고 해요. 외모를 직접 말하는 표현이라 다른 사람에게 쓸 때는 조심하는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: It describes a nose whose tip curves downward; the opposite, with an upturned tip, is '들창코'. Since it comments directly on someone's looks, be careful when using it about other people.

examples.ko: 도로 공사 전에 가스관 매설 위치를 확인해요.
examples.en: Before road work, they check where the gas pipes are laid.

examples.ko: 수도관 매설 작업 때문에 길이 막혀요.
examples.en: The road is blocked because of water pipe laying work.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 지하 케이블 매설이 거의 끝났어요.
examples.en: The underground cable laying in this area is almost done.
It is dangerous if the laying depth is too shallow.

examples.ko: 오래된 매설 배관을 새것으로 바꿀 거예요.
examples.en: They will replace the old buried pipes with new ones.

examples.ko: 땅속에 매설 공사를 하느라 소음이 커요.
examples.en: The noise is loud because of the burying work underground.

explain: 뉴스나 공사 안내문에서 '가스관 매설', '매설 공사'처럼 관, 전선, 케이블과 함께 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '땅에 묻다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It appears in news and construction notices with pipes, wires and cables, as in '가스관 매설' or '매설 공사'. In everyday talk people simply say '땅에 묻다'.

examples.ko: 시청에서 새 도로 밑에 하수관을 매설해요.
examples.en: The city hall lays a sewer pipe under the new road.
They are digging the ground and laying electric wires.

examples.ko: 이 관은 지하 2미터 깊이에 매설해야 해요.
examples.en: This pipe has to be laid two meters underground.

examples.ko: 가스관을 매설할 때는 안전 검사를 꼭 해요.
examples.en: When laying gas pipes, they always do a safety inspection.
They laid communication lines on this street last year.
Where would be a good place to lay the drain pipe?

explain: 관, 전선, 케이블처럼 길게 이어진 시설을 땅속에 설치할 때 써요. 공사 보고서나 뉴스에서 주로 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '묻다'를 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used for long installations like pipes, wires and cables put underground. You mostly see it in construction reports and the news; in daily talk people use '묻다'.

examples.ko: 이 나라는 석유 매장량이 세계에서 가장 많아요.
examples.en: This country has the largest oil reserves in the world.

examples.ko: 새로 발견된 가스 매장량은 얼마나 돼요?
examples.en: How large are the newly found gas reserves?
Coal reserves are gradually shrinking.
Experts are surveying the deposits of the mine.

examples.ko: 매장량이 많아도 개발 비용이 비싸면 소용없어요.
examples.en: Even with large reserves, it is no use if development costs too much.
Compared with the reserves, production is very small.

explain: 땅속에 묻혀 있는 석유, 석탄, 가스 같은 자원의 양에 써요. '매장량이 풍부하다/적다'처럼 말하고, 가게를 뜻하는 '매장'과는 소리만 같아요.
explain_en: It is used for the amount of resources such as oil, coal and gas underground, as in '매장량이 풍부하다/적다'. It only sounds the same as '매장' meaning a shop.

examples.ko: 마스크 매점매석 때문에 값이 크게 올랐어요.
examples.en: Prices rose a lot because of mask hoarding.
The government announced it would crack down on hoarding.
Hoarding goods to push up prices is illegal.

examples.ko: 매점매석 행위가 늘어서 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Hoarding has increased, so it often appears in the news.
When rice prices went up, hoarding increased.

examples.ko: 매점매석으로 돈을 번 상인이 벌을 받았어요.
examples.en: The merchant who made money by hoarding was punished.

explain: 경제 뉴스에서 '매점매석 단속'처럼 많이 나오는 말이고, 가격을 올리려는 업자나 상인의 행동에 주로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '사재기'를 훨씬 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It appears in economic news as in '매점매석 단속', mostly about dealers or merchants trying to push prices up. In daily conversation people use '사재기' much more often.

examples.ko: 매제는 우리 집에서 가까운 곳에 살아요.
examples.en: My sister's husband lives close to our house.
My younger sister and her husband are visiting this weekend.
I introduced a new job to my sister's husband.
I often go fishing with my younger sister's husband.

examples.ko: 이번 명절에는 매제도 같이 오기로 했어요.
examples.en: My brother-in-law is coming too this holiday.
We call a younger sister's husband a 'maeje'.

explain: 남자가 여동생의 남편을 가리킬 때 써요. 여자는 같은 사람을 '제부'라고 불러요. 남자가 누나의 남편을 부를 때는 '매형', 여자가 언니의 남편을 부를 때는 '형부'라고 해서 말이 서로 달라요.
explain_en: A man uses it for his younger sister's husband; a woman calls the same person '제부'. A man calls his older sister's husband '매형', and a woman calls her older sister's husband '형부', so the words differ.

examples.en: The smell of burning trash is acrid.
The air was so smoky that I opened the window.

examples.ko: 불난 곳 근처는 매캐한 냄새가 가득했어요.
examples.en: The area near the fire was full of an acrid smell.
My throat hurts because of the acrid dust.
I burned the meat, and now the house smells smoky.

examples.ko: 문을 닫았더니 방 안이 더 매캐해졌어요.
examples.en: After I closed the door, the room became even more smoky.

explain: 연기나 탄 냄새, 먼지가 코와 목을 따갑게 자극하는 느낌에 써요. 곰팡이 냄새 같은 '퀴퀴하다'와는 달라요.
explain_en: It describes smoke, burnt smells or dust that stings the nose and throat. It differs from '퀴퀴하다', which is a musty, moldy smell.

examples.en: Whether you do it or not, the result is the same.

examples.ko: 비싼 옷이든 싼 옷이든 입으면 매한가지예요.
examples.en: Whether the clothes are expensive or cheap, once you wear them it's all the same.

examples.ko: 알고도 말 안 했으면 나도 매한가지잖아요.
examples.en: If I knew and didn't say anything, I'm just as bad, aren't I?

examples.ko: 지금 가나 나중에 가나 매한가지 아니에요?
examples.en: Isn't it the same whether you go now or later?

examples.ko: 둘 다 힘든 건 매한가지라서 그냥 골랐어요.
examples.en: Both are equally hard, so I just picked one.
Adults and kids alike get sleepy.

explain: '~나 ~나 매한가지예요'나 '~도 매한가지예요'처럼 서로 다른 둘이 결국 같다고 말할 때 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '마찬가지'를 훨씬 더 자주 쓰고, 매한가지는 조금 예스럽고 구어적인 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used in patterns like '~나 ~나 매한가지예요' to say two different things turn out to be the same. '마찬가지' is much more common for this meaning, while 매한가지 sounds a bit old-fashioned and colloquial.

examples.en: I bought and ate elvan-roasted eggs at the market.

examples.ko: 맥반석 오징어는 고소해서 영화 볼 때 좋아요.
examples.en: Elvan-roasted squid is savory and good for watching movies.
I went to a sauna with elvan stone floors.

examples.ko: 맥반석 위에서 구운 고구마가 정말 달아요.
examples.en: Sweet potatoes roasted on elvan stones are really sweet.
I sweated a lot in the elvan sauna.

examples.ko: 맥반석으로 만든 그릇에 밥을 지어 봤어요.
examples.en: I cooked rice in a pot made of elvan stone.

explain: 일상에서는 '맥반석 계란', '맥반석 오징어'처럼 구이 음식 이름이나 찜질방 간판에서 자주 보여요. 돌 이름이지만 먹거리와 함께 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: In daily life you mostly see it in food names like '맥반석 계란' and '맥반석 오징어', or on sauna signs. It is a stone name, but often appears with food.

examples.en: Since morning, he answered in a listless voice.

examples.ko: 시험에 떨어져서 그런지 오늘 표정이 맥없어요.
examples.en: Maybe because of failing the exam, your face looks listless today.

examples.ko: 맥없어 보여서 무슨 일 있냐고 물었어요.
examples.en: You looked so listless that I asked if something was wrong.
Worn out by the heat, his steps were weak.

examples.ko: 맥없던 아이가 간식을 먹고 기운을 차렸어요.
examples.en: The listless child perked up after eating a snack.
If you feel that drained, rest early today.

explain: 사람의 표정, 목소리, 걸음처럼 기운이 빠진 모습을 말할 때 써요. '힘없다'보다 축 처진 느낌이 강하고, 부사 '맥없이'와 함께 외워 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It describes a drained look in a person's expression, voice or walk. It feels more droopy than '힘없다', and it helps to learn it together with the adverb '맥없이'.

examples.en: He slumped limply into the chair.
We lost meekly to the other team.
I saw the player collapse limply.
The child nodded weakly.

examples.ko: 맥없이 앉아 있지 말고 좀 움직여요.
examples.en: Don't just sit there limply; move around a bit.
I laughed weakly after hearing I had passed.

explain: '맥없이 지다', '맥없이 쓰러지다', '맥없이 주저앉다'처럼 쓰이고, 특히 경기에서 제대로 싸워 보지도 못하고 질 때 자주 말해요. '힘없이'보다 기운이 확 빠진 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It appears in phrases like '맥없이 지다', '맥없이 쓰러지다' and '맥없이 주저앉다', and is often used for losing a game without putting up a fight. It feels more drained than '힘없이'.

examples.en: There were no side dishes, so I ate only plain rice.
Even plain rice is really tasty when freshly cooked.

examples.ko: 아이가 맨밥을 싫어해서 김에 싸 줬어요.
examples.en: My child doesn't like plain rice, so I wrapped it in seaweed.

examples.ko: 입맛이 없을 때는 맨밥에 김치만 먹어요.
examples.en: When I have no appetite, I eat just rice with kimchi.

examples.ko: 맨밥 한 공기랑 계란 프라이면 충분해요.
examples.en: A bowl of plain rice and a fried egg are enough.
I made rice balls with the leftover plain rice.

explain: '맨-'은 아무것도 더하지 않은 상태를 나타내서 맨손, 맨발과 같은 짝이에요. 맨밥은 반찬 없이 먹는 밥이나 다른 것을 섞지 않은 밥에 써요.
explain_en: The prefix '맨-' means nothing added, like in 맨손 (bare hands) and 맨발 (bare feet). 맨밥 is rice eaten without side dishes, or rice with nothing mixed in.

examples.en: I feel bad asking my friend for a favor without offering anything.

examples.ko: 아침에 맨입으로 약을 먹으면 속이 쓰릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: Taking medicine on an empty stomach in the morning can upset your stomach.
You want me to help you move for nothing?

examples.ko: 맨입으로 가기 뭐해서 과일을 사 갔어요.
examples.en: It felt awkward to go empty-handed, so I bought some fruit.

examples.ko: 맨입이니까 커피보다 물부터 마시는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: Since your stomach is empty, drink water before coffee.

examples.ko: 맨입 상태로 운동하면 어지러울 수 있어요.
examples.en: Exercising on an empty stomach can make you dizzy.

explain: '맨입으로 안 되죠'처럼 아무 대가나 선물 없이 부탁하는 것을 말할 때 많이 써요. 아무것도 먹지 않은 빈속이라는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: It is often used as in '맨입으로 안 되죠' (you can't ask for that for nothing), meaning without any payment or gift. It can also mean having eaten nothing, an empty stomach.

examples.en: He started from nothing and grew the company.
It's hard to beat a big opponent with bare fists alone.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 맨주먹 하나로 챔피언이 됐어요.
examples.en: That boxer became a champion with just his bare fists.

examples.ko: 우리는 돈 한 푼 없는 맨주먹 신세였어요.
examples.en: We were empty-handed, without a penny.
I clenched my bare fists and made up my mind.
A story that began from nothing was made into a movie.

explain: 아무것도 쥐지 않은 주먹을 말하지만, 일상에서는 가진 것 없이 시작하는 상황에 더 많이 써요. '맨손', '빈손'과 비슷한 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 그분은 맨주먹으로 시작해서 큰 회사를 만들었어요.
phrases.en: He started with nothing and built a big company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주먹이 아니라 돈이나 도움 없이 처음부터 시작한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means starting with no money or help, not literally using fists.

explain_en: It literally means a fist holding nothing, but in daily life it is used more for starting with nothing. It feels close to '맨손' and '빈손'.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 맷돌로 콩을 갈아 두부를 만들었어요.
examples.en: In the old days, people ground beans with a millstone to make tofu.

examples.ko: 할머니 집 마당에 오래된 맷돌이 있어요.
examples.en: There is an old millstone in my grandmother's yard.

examples.ko: 맷돌을 돌릴 때는 손잡이를 잡아야 해요.
examples.en: When turning a millstone, you have to hold the handle.
I learned how to use a millstone at the museum.

examples.ko: 맷돌에 간 콩으로 만든 두부는 맛이 달라요.
examples.en: Tofu made from beans ground on a millstone tastes different.

examples.ko: 맷돌처럼 생긴 돌 탁자에서 차를 마셨어요.
examples.en: I had tea at a stone table shaped like a millstone.

explain: 곡식이나 콩을 가는 옛 도구라서 요즘은 박물관, 전통 음식점, 시골집에서 볼 수 있어요. 지금은 믹서로 가니까 '맷돌에 갈다'는 옛날 방식이나 전통 방식을 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It is an old tool for grinding grain and beans, so today you see it in museums, traditional restaurants and country homes. Since people now use blenders, '맷돌에 갈다' refers to the old or traditional way.

examples.ko: 그 복서는 맷집이 좋아서 잘 안 쓰러져요.
examples.en: That boxer can take a lot of hits, so he rarely goes down.
I built up my toughness through exercise, so it hurts less.

examples.ko: 맷집이 약해서 작은 비판에도 마음이 흔들려요.
examples.en: I'm thin-skinned, so even small criticism shakes me.

examples.ko: 오랜 회사 생활로 맷집이 많이 늘었어요.
examples.en: After years at work, my resilience has grown a lot.

examples.ko: 맷집 좋은 신입이 들어와서 팀이 든든해요.
examples.en: A tough new hire joined, so the team feels reassured.
There's a limit to just toughing it out.

explain: 원래는 맞아도 잘 견디는 몸의 힘을 말했는데, 요즘은 비판이나 실패를 견디는 마음의 힘에도 많이 써요. '맷집이 좋다/세다/약하다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It originally meant the body's ability to take hits, but now it is also used for the mental strength to endure criticism or failure. People say '맷집이 좋다/세다/약하다'.

examples.en: The government changed its stance under the opposition's fierce attack.
Our team launched a fierce attack in the second half.

examples.ko: 상대 팀의 맹공을 잘 막아 냈어요.
examples.en: We held off the other team's fierce attack well.
The candidates attacked each other fiercely.
After the press conference, harsh attacks poured onto the politician.

examples.ko: 신제품이 경쟁사의 맹공 속에서도 잘 팔렸어요.
examples.en: The new product sold well even amid the rival's aggressive push.

explain: 스포츠 경기나 정치 뉴스에서 공격이나 비판을 강하게 몰아붙일 때 써요. '맹공을 퍼붓다/가하다/받다'처럼 짝말로 외워 두세요.
explain_en: It is used in sports and political news when attacks or criticism are pressed hard. Learn it as a set phrase: '맹공을 퍼붓다/가하다/받다'.

examples.en: This snake has a deadly venom.
Pufferfish eggs contain a deadly poison.
I heard a highly venomous jellyfish appeared on the beach.

examples.ko: 맹독 때문에 이 식물은 만지면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Because of its deadly poison, you must not touch this plant.
Many scientists study the nature of this deadly poison.

examples.ko: 맹독에 중독되면 바로 병원에 가야 해요.
examples.en: If you are poisoned by a deadly toxin, go to the hospital right away.

explain: 그냥 '독'보다 훨씬 강하고 위험한 독을 말할 때 써요. 뱀, 복어, 해파리, 식물처럼 자연 속 위험한 생물을 설명할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to poison much stronger and more dangerous than plain '독'. It often appears when describing hazardous creatures and plants such as snakes, pufferfish, jellyfish and plants.

examples.ko: 다섯 살짜리가 어른에게 따지다니 참 맹랑해요.
examples.en: A five-year-old arguing with an adult is quite cheeky.
Everyone laughed thanks to the cheeky little kid.

examples.ko: 어린아이가 말을 어찌나 맹랑하게 하는지 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised at how boldly the little child spoke.

examples.ko: 신입이 사장님께 먼저 악수를 청하다니 맹랑하네요.
examples.en: A new hire offering a handshake to the boss first is pretty bold.
That child was cheekier than he looked.
I scold him for being cheeky, but he's cute too.

explain: 주로 어린아이나 아랫사람이 나이에 비해 당돌하고 야무지게 굴 때 써요. 놀라움이 섞여 있어서 '당돌하다'와 비슷하지만 귀엽다는 느낌이 들 때도 있어요.
explain_en: It is mainly used when a child or junior person acts boldly and sharply beyond their age. It carries surprise, so it is similar to '당돌하다', and can sometimes feel endearing.

examples.en: The flames are spreading fiercely.
The players ran fiercely toward the championship.
The typhoon raged so fiercely that I couldn't go out.
He studied intensely and passed.
The two candidates are confronting each other fiercely.
Our team chased hard and turned the game around.

explain: 불길, 태풍, 추격, 공부처럼 기세가 아주 강한 움직임이나 노력에 써요. 형용사 '맹렬하다'에서 나온 부사라서 '맹렬하게'보다 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is used for very forceful movement or effort, such as fire, typhoons, chasing or studying. It comes from the adjective '맹렬하다' and is more common in writing and news than '맹렬하게'.

examples.ko: 맹세코 제가 말씀드린 건 거짓말이 아니에요.
examples.en: I swear what I told you is not a lie.

examples.ko: 저는 맹세코 그 일과 아무 상관이 없어요.
examples.en: I swear I have nothing to do with that matter.
I swear I will never be late for an appointment again.

examples.ko: 맹세코 말씀드리는데 그 파일은 제가 지우지 않았어요.
examples.en: I swear to you, I didn't delete that file.
He said he would keep the secret, swearing on it.

examples.ko: 맹세코 이 맛집은 실패할 일이 없어요.
examples.en: I swear this restaurant will never let you down.

explain: 자기 말이 진짜라고 강하게 말하거나 앞으로 꼭 하겠다고 다짐할 때 문장 앞이나 주어 뒤에 써요. '정말', '진짜'보다 무겁고 강한 말투라서 가벼운 대화에서는 농담처럼 들릴 수도 있어요.
explain_en: Place it at the start of a sentence or after the subject to stress that you are telling the truth or will surely do something. It is heavier than '정말' or '진짜', so in casual talk it can sound like a joke.

examples.ko: 과학에 대한 맹신도 문제가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Blind faith in science can also be a problem.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 점에 대한 맹신이 심해요.
examples.en: He has a strong blind faith in fortune-telling.

examples.ko: 한 가지 의견만 믿는 맹신은 판단을 흐려요.
examples.en: Blind faith in just one opinion clouds your judgment.

examples.ko: 후기 맹신 때문에 실패한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I once failed because I trusted reviews blindly.

examples.ko: 유명인의 말에 대한 맹신을 버려야 해요.
examples.en: We should give up our blind trust in celebrities' words.
I broke free from blind trust and checked it myself.

explain: 믿음이 깊다는 좋은 뜻이 아니라 따져 보지 않고 무조건 믿는다는 부정적인 느낌이에요. 반대로는 '의심하다', '비판적으로 보다' 같은 말을 써요.
explain_en: It does not mean deep faith in a good sense; it is negative, implying believing without questioning. Its opposites are things like '의심하다' and '비판적으로 보다'.

examples.ko: 후기를 너무 맹신하면 실망할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you trust reviews too blindly, you may be disappointed.

examples.ko: 저는 유명 블로거의 말을 맹신하지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't blindly trust what famous bloggers say.
My parents blindly believe health food ads.

examples.ko: 친구가 한 말을 그대로 맹신해서 실수했어요.
examples.en: I blindly believed what my friend said and made a mistake.
You shouldn't blindly trust an AI's answers.
It was foolish of me to trust him blindly.

explain: '~을/를 맹신하다' 형태로 쓰고, 믿으면 안 되는 것을 따져 보지 않고 믿는다는 비판의 느낌이 있어요. 부정형 '맹신하지 마세요'처럼 조언할 때도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is used as '~을/를 맹신하다' and carries a note of criticism, believing something without questioning. It is also common in advice like '맹신하지 마세요' (don't trust blindly).

examples.en: The heat wave is raging this summer.
The flu raged, so school was closed.
The market opened even amid the fierce cold wave.

examples.ko: 겨울 추위가 맹위를 떨칠 때는 집에 있고 싶어요.
examples.en: When winter cold rages, I want to stay home.

examples.ko: 새로운 바이러스가 맹위를 떨칠까 봐 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I'm worried a new virus might rage.
All the street trees fell to the fury of the typhoon.

explain: 거의 '맹위를 떨치다'라는 짝말로 쓰고, 더위, 추위, 태풍, 질병처럼 사람이 막기 어려운 힘이 강할 때 써요. 사람의 성격이나 기분에는 잘 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is almost always used in the set phrase '맹위를 떨치다', for forces hard to stop such as heat, cold, typhoons and diseases. It is not used for a person's character or mood.
